result.summary: Sets SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE instead of SO_REUSEADDR on P2P listen sockets on Windows, preventing other local sockets from binding to the same port. Fails socket binding if setting the exclusive address option fails, and adds functional tests covering both binding conflict orderings.
result.problem: On Windows, SO_REUSEADDR semantics allow another process running under the same user account to bind to an in-use port if it also sets SO_REUSEADDR. This permits a local process to intercept incoming P2P connections intended for bitcoind.
evidence: PR description cites Microsoft Winsock documentation: on Windows, SO_REUSEADDR permits a second socket to bind a port already in use by another process under the same user account unless SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE is set.
Follows merged PR #36169, which applied the same SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE fix to the RPC/HTTP listener on Windows.
result.changed_since_previous: Added a functional test checking the reverse ordering: verifying that bitcoind fails during startup if another process is already bound to its P2P listen port.
result.card: Sets SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE instead of SO_REUSEADDR on P2P listen sockets on Windows and adds functional tests for port exclusivity. On Windows, default SO_REUSEADDR semantics allow another process under the same user account to bind to an active port and intercept incoming P2P connections. This extends socket exclusivity protections previously merged for RPC listeners in PR #36169.

risk.why: If SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE fails or behaves unexpectedly on certain Windows configurations, bitcoind will fail to bind the P2P socket and refuse to start.
